details:
I’m writing to request a feature that would allow Udon scripts to access pixel data from Unity Camera components placed within a world.

This request is not about the player's head-mounted view or handheld cameras, but rather cameras intentionally set up in the environment as part of the world.

Being able to retrieve pixel data from a placed camera feels like a natural capability in a 3D platform. The fact that this is currently impossible through Udon feels quite limiting and unnatural, given how integral such a feature is for advanced interaction.

With this functionality, creators could build systems like image-based authentication, visual logic gates, or even mechanisms where avatars transmit information to the world via visible cues.

I understand that you may be focusing development efforts on Soba or future platforms. However, I believe that basic creative functionality like this should not be postponed indefinitely as a result.

Even a read-only and sandbox-safe implementation would unlock a wide range of powerful and safe use cases for world creators.

Thank you for considering this request.

Best regards,
title: Access to In-World Camera Pixel Data via Udon
